decision:
Overturn CONFIRMED: OPEN -> STANDS.

The audit graded OPEN for one reason only: the source was unread. I re-read arXiv:2606.22531v2 myself through alphaXiv this pass. One caveat on the version: the PDF the tool serves as v2 carries the page-1 stamp 'arXiv:2606.22531v1 [gr-qc] 21 Jun 2026', so I cannot tell whether I read v1 or v2.

What Le prints, Sec. VII A, p.7:
- Eq (15): sigma_0 = (1/4piR)(1 - sqrt(1-x)).
- Eq (16): p_0 = (1/8piR)((1 - x/2)/sqrt(1-x) - 1).
- Eq (17): 8piR(sigma_0 - p_0) s = -5/2 s^2 + 3s - 1/2 = -1/2(5s-1)(s-1), 'positive iff 1/5 < s < 1'.
- Eq (18): surface dec <=> x = 2m/R < 24/25.
- Lemma 1: strict wec/dec on (0, 24/25).

Elsewhere in the paper:
- App. B, p.18, restates the margin as (B1) = (1/2)(1-s)(5s-1). Its K^theta_theta = sqrt(f)/R and K^tau_tau = f'/(2 sqrt f) match the audit's C1.
- Sec. XIV, p.17, prints the clause wall.py quotes word for word; wall.py adds one comma, after 'stiffer'.
- App. H, p.23, scopes that clause to the equilibrium margin: 'sigma_0 - p_0 is junction-fixed (a function of x alone) and independent of eta'.

Re-runs, all copied into adjudicate/run/ and all exit 0:
- The audit's rederivation (C1-C8, including the z3 window proof).
- Verifier 2's adversarial mutation and negation guards.
- Verifier 1's check of the printed form.
- My own adj_check.py (sympy). It shows that Le's (15)-(16) give his (17) exactly and that (B1) is the same expression. The tree's form equals Le's (17) divided by s, which equals 8piR(sigma_0 - p_0). v4's (2.13) equals sigma_0 - p_0. The tree's form is NOT literally Le's (17), which carries an extra factor s on its left-hand side. The roots are s = 1/5 and s = 1, and s = 1/5 means x = 24/25.
- wall.py --selftest.

The verifiers shared no error. All three read the same document, and I confirmed what it prints independently. Their one shared caveat, the v1/v2 stamp, does not move the content: v4 (13 Sep 2026) prints the same margin as Eq (2.13), with the same window.

No empirical datum enters the result. Le himself places the 24/25 window as the flat-interior case of earlier rigorous thin-shell bounds: Andreasson [50] and Horvat-Ilijic [51], whose general sharp DEC bound is 48/49 [52]. Those works are named in Le and were not read here.

Why STANDS and not NARROWED: the tree drops no hypothesis that Le states. Le states the result for the static flat-interior/Schwarzschild anchor. The static-equilibrium and lambda = 0 limits are Le's own as well as the tree's: App. H gives the first, and App. E/Sec. XIV say 'the outgoing mass-loss flux ... tightens the surface dec margin'.
scope:
The grade covers:
- The static thin-shell margin for a Minkowski interior matched to a Schwarzschild exterior: 8piR(sigma_0 - p_0) = -(5s-1)(s-1)/(2s), with s = sqrt(1-x) and 0 < x < 1.
- The window: strict surface dec iff 0 < x < 24/25, with zero margin at x = 24/25.
- The equilibrium margin's independence of the equation-of-state slope.
- The attribution to Le v2 Eq (17), up to the factor-s rearrangement and the v1/v2 stamp caveat.

It does NOT cover:
- (a) An oscillating or off-equilibrium wall, whose margin depends on beta^2 at first order (audit C7).
- (b) The radiating lambda = aR > 0 wall, whose window shrinks under Le's envelope (29), which is empirical (warpshell.py:91).
- (c) The tangential-pressure thick wall (the 4/5 window).
- (d) Any stability claim the tree builds on the 'stiffer wall' clause, including v4's growing modes and ill-posedness. Those belong to the stability-clause audit.

Andreasson and Horvat-Ilijic are named, not read.
corrections_to_record: The audit's read_status NAMED-NOT-READ and agrees_with_source 'not-run' are superseded. The source is now READ and agrees: Le v2 p.7 (Eqs 15-18, Lemma 1), p.18 (B1), p.17 (Sec XIV), p.23 (App H).

Version caveat: the PDF alphaXiv serves as 2606.22531v2 is stamped 'arXiv:2606.22531v1 [gr-qc] 21 Jun 2026' on p.1, while the tree cites v2 (30 June 2026). Which version was read cannot be told apart. The content does not change: v4 (13 Sep 2026, retitled 'Radiative steering of warp shells') prints the same margin as Eq (2.13), (1-s)(5s-1)/(16 pi R s), with strict DEC for 0<x<24/25.
Equation numbering: 'Eq (17)' is the v1/v2 number. In v4 the same equation is Eq (2.13).

Discrepancy of form, not of value: Le prints Eq (17) as 8piR(sigma_0-p_0) s = -1/2(5s-1)(s-1), with a factor s on the left-hand side. The tree's '-(5s-1)(s-1)/(2s)' (wall.py:46, 265, 269-271) is that equation divided by s>0. So wall.py:269's 'Le's printed closed form' is a rearrangement, not a transcription.
The quotation at wall.py:11-14 is word for word Le Sec XIV p.17, except that wall.py adds a comma after 'stiffer'.
Window edge wording: Le's 'surface dec <=> x<24/25' is the STRICT condition. Non-strict dec holds on 0<x<=24/25.

Two named scope hypotheses are carried, and neither is grounds to narrow. Static equilibrium: Le App H calls the margin 'a function of x alone', and off equilibrium the margin depends on beta^2 (audit C7). lambda=0: Le App E/Sec XIV say the mass-loss flux tightens the margin, and Le calls envelope (29) 'physically motivated', i.e. empirical.

The vacuous self-check at wall.py:527-528 stands as recorded. It builds a one-element set {round(dec_margin_scaled(0.3),12)}, never varies beta^2, and so passes for any input. The claim it guards still holds by construction.

Earlier literature: Le v2 p.8 places the window as the flat-interior case of Andreasson [50] and Horvat-Ilijic [51], whose general sharp DEC bound is 48/49 [52]. v4 calls it 'the familiar flat-interior compactness bound' [25,26]. None of these was read here, so they carry no weight in the grade. The audit's later_literature value 'contested' was an enum placeholder and should read 'confirms (as cited by the source; not read)'.
